15 new stories in the Rochdale borough since yesterday morning.

The stories

  • Man jailed for over a decade for role in Rochdale drug supply Rochdale
    A man has been sentenced to 12 years in prison for his involvement in the supply of Class A drugs across Rochdale.
  • Rochdale man who managed 'Adam' drug line dealers jailed for 10 and a half years Rochdale
    Haider Ali, 34, of Pike Street, was sentenced at Minshull Street Crown Court on Monday 9 November after an investigation that began with a drug deal on Baron Street.
  • Police warn of rising family gold burglaries in Rochdale and surrounding areas Rochdale
    Greater Manchester Police have reported an increase in family gold burglaries, urging residents to remain vigilant as winter approaches.
  • Police warn Rochdale homes to lock away family gold after rise in burglaries Rochdale
    Burglaries targeting family gold have risen in Rochdale, Oldham and Bury in recent weeks, mostly at weekends, with entry usually gained at the rear of homes.
  • Comment: Should fireworks be allowed on any night but bonfire night? Rochdale
    Rochdale's council displays went quiet this year, but residents say fireworks carried on into this week. We look at the law, the harm to people and animals, and what could change.
  • Volunteers wanted for Rochdale town centre's Saturday night Safe Haven Rochdale
    Community Medics is recruiting welfare volunteers aged 16 and over for its town centre welfare point, which runs on Saturday nights from 10pm to 3am. Training is provided.
  • Free job-search, CV and money advice at Middleton Library today Middleton
    Middleton Library is hosting a free work and skills hub on Monday 9 November, with help for job applications, interviews and managing budgets.
  • Free Heywood Library friendship group offers a place to meet people this Thursday Heywood
    A free drop-in friendship group at Heywood Library on Thursday 12 November is open to adults, with no advance booking required.
  • Rochdale South Township Committee meets on Wednesday: when and where Rochdale
    Rochdale South Township Committee is scheduled to meet at Number One Riverside on Wednesday 11 November. Here is how residents can check the agenda.
  • School-run parking in Rochdale: what can the council do? Rochdale
    The council has stepped up patrols outside schools and is consulting on School Streets. New pavement parking powers are on the way from the government.
  • Cranmer Education Trust staff gather for professional development event Middleton
    Staff from Cranmer Education Trust, which operates schools in Middleton and Oldham, convened for a professional development event aimed at improving children's lives through inclusive education.
  • Littleborough pub launches new pool league to strengthen community ties Littleborough
    Admiral Taverns pub in Littleborough invites local venues to join a new pool league, fostering community spirit and competition among players.

Weather: Cloudy 8°C in Rochdale today.

The Morning Briefing is published every day at 9am. Got a story? Tell the newsdesk.
body:
15 new stories in the Rochdale borough since yesterday morning.

The stories:

Man jailed for over a decade for role in Rochdale drug supply (Rochdale). A man has been sentenced to 12 years in prison for his involvement in the supply of Class A drugs across Rochdale.

Rochdale man who managed 'Adam' drug line dealers jailed for 10 and a half years (Rochdale). Haider Ali, 34, of Pike Street, was sentenced at Minshull Street Crown Court on Monday 9 November after an investigation that began with a drug deal on Baron Street.

Police warn of rising family gold burglaries in Rochdale and surrounding areas (Rochdale). Greater Manchester Police have reported an increase in family gold burglaries, urging residents to remain vigilant as winter approaches.

Police warn Rochdale homes to lock away family gold after rise in burglaries (Rochdale). Burglaries targeting family gold have risen in Rochdale, Oldham and Bury in recent weeks, mostly at weekends, with entry usually gained at the rear of homes.

Comment: Should fireworks be allowed on any night but bonfire night? (Rochdale). Rochdale's council displays went quiet this year, but residents say fireworks carried on into this week. We look at the law, the harm to people and animals, and what could change.

Volunteers wanted for Rochdale town centre's Saturday night Safe Haven (Rochdale). Community Medics is recruiting welfare volunteers aged 16 and over for its town centre welfare point, which runs on Saturday nights from 10pm to 3am. Training is provided.

Free job-search, CV and money advice at Middleton Library today (Middleton). Middleton Library is hosting a free work and skills hub on Monday 9 November, with help for job applications, interviews and managing budgets.

Free Heywood Library friendship group offers a place to meet people this Thursday (Heywood). A free drop-in friendship group at Heywood Library on Thursday 12 November is open to adults, with no advance booking required.

Rochdale South Township Committee meets on Wednesday: when and where (Rochdale). Rochdale South Township Committee is scheduled to meet at Number One Riverside on Wednesday 11 November. Here is how residents can check the agenda.

School-run parking in Rochdale: what can the council do? (Rochdale). The council has stepped up patrols outside schools and is consulting on School Streets. New pavement parking powers are on the way from the government.

Cranmer Education Trust staff gather for professional development event (Middleton). Staff from Cranmer Education Trust, which operates schools in Middleton and Oldham, convened for a professional development event aimed at improving children's lives through inclusive education.

Littleborough pub launches new pool league to strengthen community ties (Littleborough). Admiral Taverns pub in Littleborough invites local venues to join a new pool league, fostering community spirit and competition among players.

Weather: Cloudy 8°C in Rochdale today.

The Morning Briefing is published every day at 9am. Got a story? Tell the newsdesk.
